title: Customer degradation rehearsal and briefing kit
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact kit for organizing and running customer-facing degradation rehearsals (aka 'customer drills'). The goal: let customers experience our fallback modalities in a controlled setting, validate SLOs/expectations, and give Sales/CS/SEs scripts and artifacts they can use during real incidents.

Audience:
- Customer success managers (CSMs)
- Solutions engineers (SEs) and pre-sales
- Account execs (AEs) for enterprise customers
- Product & Incident comms owners

High-level approach (30/60/90 minute options):
- 30m quick demo: walk through a single-mode fallback (model downgrade -> cached responses) and run customer Q&A.
- 60m technical+comms: replicate degraded capacity, trigger multi-region routing, validate response timeliness and quality with a small prompt suite.
- 90m end-to-end drill: include customer routing policies, console walkthrough (observability), and a short post-drill retrospective with follow-ups.

Pre-run checklist (owner initials):
- Invite list & incident roles (SE lead, CSM lead, Eng pager): ________
- Test tenant with realistic traffic (masked sample data): ________
- Backup model variants deployed (quantized & smaller arch): ________
- Multi-region routes ready (primary, secondary): ________
- Notifications template prepared (email + in-console banner): ________
- Scripted prompts (5-10) that represent customer workload: ________
- Observability hooks (tracing + token/time breakdowns): ________

Runbook (scripted steps for SE/CS during rehearsal):
1) Kickoff (5m)
  - Opening line: "Today we're running a controlled scenario to see how Redwood handles reduced capacity while preserving availability. You'll see how we fall back to a compatible model and route traffic to an alternate region."
  - Confirm scope: what we'll simulate (latency, model unavailability, region failover).
2) Step 1: Simulate reduced GPU slots (engineering toggles) (10m)
  - Observe console: spike in queueing, then automatic routing to fallback model variant.
  - SE talking points: "You may see slightly different phrasing — we prioritize staying online and predictable latency over some marginal quality changes."
3) Step 2: Trigger model substitution (10m)
  - Show side-by-side generation: primary model vs fallback (short examples).
  - CS talking points: "Fallback models are validated for your workload during onboarding; we recommend a canary prompt set to measure differences."
4) Step 3: Multi-region failover (10m)
  - Trigger region route policy; demonstrate session continuity where KV cache behavior allows partial warm-start.
  - Talking points on data residency: "We only fail over to allowed regions in your policy; for Private mode we will not cross your VPC without explicit config."
5) Q&A and live adjustments (15m)
  - Capture customer concerns, thresholds they'd accept for graceful degradation.
6) Retrospective (10m)
  - Action items, open questions, follow-up demo dates.

Incident narratives: short soundbites and lengthier scripts
- Soundbite: "We kept your app online by routing to a compatible model and an alternate region; you may notice slight wording changes but no downtime."
- SE script (technical): "We observed sustained queue depth on primary pools and engaged the fallback policy. Requests were automatically routed to the quantized 13B variant with equivalent prompt mapping; throughput returned to target within X sec. We'll follow up with request-level logs and token-level cost delta."
- Exec script (customer-facing): "Redwood prioritized availability: we substituted to an alternative model variant and routed traffic to a secondary region to avoid interruptions. We're sharing an incident summary and this replay so you can validate the impact."

Messaging templates (short + long):
- Short in-app banner: "Service operating in safe-mode: routing to fallback models to preserve availability. Expect minor quality variance."
- Customer email (concise): "We ran a controlled mitigation for your tenant at HH:MM UTC — traffic routed to an alternate model/region to preserve service. No data was lost. Attached: short report and next steps."
- Post-drill report outline (1-pager): incident summary, triggers simulated, observed SLOs (latency, error rate), quality checks (prompt set comparisons), recommended follow-ups.

Quality & validation guidance (for SEs):
- Always run a 20–30 prompt canary across primary+fallback before approving the fallback path for a customer. Keep canary prompts representative (edge cases, hallucination-sensitive prompts).
- Track: latency p50/p95/p99, generation token delta, embedding cosine shifts (if used), and gross content regressions flagged by evals.

Competitive notes (how to position Redwood during the drill):
- Talk track: Redwood gives customers explicit control over where we will route during a degradation, plus transparent token-level cost/latency tradeoffs.
- Distinguish from managed endpoints that simply queue or throttle: we proactively substitute validated model variants to keep apps responsive.
- Against pure self-hosted vendors: emphasize we provide built-in, observable fallbacks without the customer rebuilding their routing/rollback logic.

Customer objections & rebuttals (quick):
- "We can't accept cross-region failover." -> "We won't fail over to a region you haven't authorized; for Private we respect VPC constraints and KMS boundaries."
- "Model outputs differ too much." -> "We can pre-approve a model family and run a prompt gating policy — fallback only triggers for prompts where semantic equivalence is validated."
- "Concerned about cost impact." -> "We include token-level deltas in the post-drill report and can configure thresholds to prefer cheaper paths for non-critical requests."

Incident follow-ups & triage backlog items to capture during drill:
- Which prompts produced unacceptable regressions? (tag and add to eval suite)
- Which customers want stricter routing policies (region-only, model pins)?
- SLA language clarifications needed for Dedicated/Private tiers?

Metrics to capture during the rehearsal (minimum):
- Time to first successful response after trigger (sec)
- Percentage of sessions routed to fallback model
- Average delta in cost per 1k tokens for routed requests
- Quality regressions flagged (binary counts)

Operational knobs and how to explain them to customers:
- Routing policy: latency-first | cost-first | region-locked (explain tradeoffs simply).
- Model pinning: per-route pin to exact model version or model family fallback.
- Canary gating: maximum allowed divergence score before we block fallback.

Rehearsal calendar template (send to customer):
- Week 0: alignment call (30m) – scope and safety checks
- Week 1: staging rehearsal (60m) – internal only (Redwood + customer engineering)
- Week 2: customer-facing drill (60–90m)
- Week 2+: optional follow-up (30m) – review artifacts, sign off on fallback policy

Artifacts to deliver after the drill (attach to ticket):
- One-page replay with timelines (png/svg export from console)
- Sample generation diffs for canary prompts (csv)
- Action item list with owners and due dates
- Configuration snippet customers can use to lock policies (YAML)

Notes for internal enablement (SE trainings):
- Practice talking about quality/latency as tradeoffs, not failures. Use phrases like "measured variance" and "validated substitute".
- Role-play scenarios: AE handles procurement/contract questions, SE handles technical safe-mode guarantees, CSM handles expectations and SLA clarifications.

Appendix: quick FAQ (short answers)
Q: Will our data leave the configured geography?
A: Not unless you explicitly authorize cross-region failover; Private tenants never cross your VPC boundary without explicit config.

Q: How do you validate a fallback model?
A: We run a customer-specific canary set during onboarding + periodic regression evals; fallbacks are only marked 'compatible' once they meet pre-defined thresholds.

Q: Can customers opt out of automatic fallbacks?
A: Yes — we support manual failover, strict model pins, and region-locking. This is a tradeoff between availability and consistent outputs.

Open questions to resolve before next draft:
- Define exact divergence threshold metric we'll use in customer-facing language (semantic-similarity % or custom eval score?).
- Standardize the CSV format for generation diffs for CSMs to share with customers.

End of kit.
